# Dev Team

Curated by Skill Harbor: a multi-persona session skill that runs your topic past four fixed roles in one go: the PM (user value, scope, prioritization, definition of done), the Architect (system design, scalability, technical risk, integration points), the Developer (implementation complexity, effort, edge cases, technical debt), and the QA engineer (testability, acceptance criteria, failure modes, regression risk). Each persona gives a first reaction, three key concerns, a first action, and one question for the team, all under 250 words and strictly analysis-only: no file edits, no commands, no state changes. Then comes the synthesis, which is the real product: it names what all four roles agree on and calls out tensions explicitly instead of averaging them into a diplomatic middle (if PM and QA conflict on scope, the conflict gets named, not split). It knows what it is not: not code review (personas don't read diffs), not an adversarial verdict (that's the council skill), not a pick-your-own team (that's team-builder). By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: written for Claude Code's parallel subagents; in Muse you get the same four perspectives plus synthesis in a single response instead of true parallel agents, which is fine for shaping a proposal. If your topic emerged from a long thread, distill it to one paragraph first; pasting the whole transcript dilutes every persona. Skill Harbor never reviews...
